segments.title: Chương 56: 0056【Yu Hua, Đứng Lại】
segments.content:
It was still three months until the fifth major speed-up of China's railways.

For Chen Guiliang to travel from Rongcheng to Modu by train, it would take at least 45 hours. A hard seat was out of the question. It would make you want to spend the rest of your life standing.

A plane was unnecessary.

Chen Guiliang bought a soft sleeper ticket. He would arrive the following day, just in time for the competition.

It was an ordinary soft sleeper with four berths.

But at the departure station, only two people boarded: Chen Guiliang and a middle-aged man.

The middle-aged man took off his coat, revealing a woolen sweater underneath. He wore gold-rimmed glasses, and his briefcase sat on top of his suitcase. He looked refined and well-educated, probably on a business trip.

"Hello."

"Hello."

After nodding and greeting each other, they each climbed onto their bunks to lie down.

Chen Guiliang took out his MP3 player and listened to the songs Bian Guanyue had downloaded, falling asleep a short while later.

When he woke again, it was nearly evening.

The middle-aged man asked, "Young man, are you going to the dining car to eat?"

"Let's go together," Chen Guiliang said, flipping over and getting out of bed.

The middle-aged man had actually intended to go to the dining car by himself and ask Chen Guiliang to watch his luggage. He figured Chen Guiliang was a student and should be relatively trustworthy.

On second thought, the soft sleeper was quite safe. The middle-aged man decided not to worry about his suitcase and just took his briefcase with him to eat.

He even stood at the door to wait for Chen Guiliang to go together.

Chen Guiliang took out four eggs and handed two to the middle-aged man.

His aunt had boiled 20 eggs for him, more than he could eat by himself.

"Thank you," the middle-aged man said as he accepted the eggs. "Young man, traveling during the winter break?"

Chen Guiliang gave a vague reply, "Something like that. Are you on a business trip, uncle?"

"Yes, a business trip," the middle-aged man answered casually.

The dining car was right next to the soft sleeper carriage.

There weren't many people there, and most of the tables were empty.

Chen Guiliang ordered a random dish. The taste was truly awful, and he could only force it down.

He had only taken a few bites when he heard someone nearby on the phone: "Hey, Mom... yeah, I'm eating in the dining car, the food is terrible... It's nothing, don't you worry... Aiya, there aren't that many bad people out there... Okay, okay, hanging up now, bye!"

The accent was thick, unique to one part of Sichuan, recognizable even to people from other provinces.

Chen Guiliang walked over with his plate. "Hey classmate, are you from Longdu?"

The speaker was a rather pretty girl with waist-length hair, looking slightly thin.

When she heard Chen Guiliang's hometown accent and got a clear look at his face, her guard dropped completely. "I am."

"Going to Modu?" Chen Guiliang asked.

The girl asked in return, "New Concept?"

Chen Guiliang stated his contestant number, "I'm A098."

"I'm A099," the girl said, standing up in pleasant surprise. She shook his hand. "My name is Mi Lan, from Shuguang (Municipal No. 2 Middle School)."

Chen Guiliang introduced himself, "Chen Guiliang, from Fu No. 2 Middle School."

Mi Lan was especially excited to meet someone from her hometown who was also participating in New Concept. "When we get back, I'll treat you to Fresh Pot Rabbit. The food on this train is so bad."

Before Chen Guiliang could agree, another boy ran over. "Did you guys just say New Concept? I'm going too!"

This accent was from Rongcheng, sounding similar to Bian Guanyue.

The boy continued, "My name is Luo Jin, from Rongcheng No. 12 Middle School, contestant number A097."

It wasn't strange for the three of them to run into each other.

This year, an exceptionally large number of people from Sichuan Province were participating in the semi-finals. In a later published collection of winning works from the New Concept competition, 16 articles from Sichuan were selected (from both Group A and Group B).

That was 8% of the total number of articles!

Most of these Sichuanese contestants were likely on this very train.

After introducing themselves, Luo Jin said to Chen Guiliang, "Guo Xiaosi is an alumnus of your school. Have you ever seen him?"

"I've seen him, but we're not close," Chen Guiliang said.

Mi Lan shared a rumor, "I was on the Mengya forum a couple of days ago, and several previous first-prize winners said they would come to the competition site to help out. We might even see Guo Xiaosi, Zhang Yueran, and the others!"

Chen Guiliang offered a humanitarian reminder, "Girls should be careful. Some people are just there to hook up."

"Hook up?" Mi Lan didn't understand the term.

Chen Guiliang explained, "They use their status as seniors and the pretense of helping to win the favor of female contestants. A man and a woman discussing literature alone in a room, with the ultimate goal of getting into bed."

Mi Lan's eyes widened. "That sort of thing happens?"

Luo Jin was also surprised. "Who did you hear that from?"

"Just be careful, that's all," Chen Guiliang said, not wanting to discuss the topic further.

They chatted for an hour, exchanged QQ numbers, and then returned to their own compartments to rest, agreeing to meet in the dining car again the next morning.

Chen Guiliang's PHS phone had no service here.

The next afternoon, they met three more contestants, all from the same school—Dafo Municipal No. 1 Middle School.

These three were all boys, staying in the same hard sleeper compartment not far from Chen Guiliang's soft sleeper.

On the afternoon of the third day, the train arrived at its destination.

Modu West Railway Station.

The hotel recommended by the competition organizers was the Qingsongcheng Hotel, about 8 kilometers from the West Station.

For convenience, Chen Guiliang wanted to take a taxi, but the other five wanted to experience the Modu subway. After asking a railway station staff member, they learned that the Modu West Station didn't have a subway line yet.

So, from Modu West Station, they first took a bus to Modu Station, then transferred to the subway to reach their destination.

They didn't even know how to buy tickets, feeling like country bumpkins in the city, which even made them a little insecure.

Chen Guiliang, who took the initiative to buy the tickets, subtly became their leader, with the other four boys and one girl following his every move.

Lei Yujie from Dafo City asked, "Chen Guiliang, have you been to Modu before?"

Chen Guiliang spouted some nonsense, "I asked how to take the subway on the Mengya forum."

"You're so thorough," Luo Jin praised.

After a short wait, the subway arrived.

The group boarded, trying to act calm, but their eyes darted around the car, looking both restrained and excited.

This was Modu!

This was the subway!

Things they had only seen in movies and read about in novels were finally before their eyes. The feeling was almost like a pilgrimage.

Mi Lan switched to Mandarin and whispered to Chen Guiliang, "I want to study here. Even if I don't get first prize, I'm still going to apply to a university in Modu!"

"I wish you success," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

Chen Xiaoping, from Dafo City, asked, "Which do you guys think is more developed, Modu or Jingcheng?"

His classmate Li Zhen said, "Probably Modu."

"I think Jingcheng is better," Luo Jin said. "I plan to apply to a university in Jingcheng."

Mi Lan asked Chen Guiliang, "What about you? Which city are you planning to go to for university? If you apply to a university in Modu too, we can travel back to Longdu together for winter and summer breaks."

"I don't really care," Chen Guiliang said truthfully.

As they spoke, the subway started moving.

Everyone quieted down, experiencing the marvel of the subway.

It seemed every vibration and sound carried the flavor of a cosmopolitan metropolis, capable of inexplicably exciting these young people from a faraway place.

Only Chen Guiliang took out his MP3 player to listen to music.

They got off the subway, asked for directions, and walked.

It was a drizzly day, and everyone had bought an umbrella just after leaving the train station.

Arriving at the Qingsongcheng Hotel lobby, they saw a sign for the New Concept competition from a distance.

There were two tables set up there where contestants needed to register. Staff would also guide them through the check-in process. Of course, they had to pay for their own rooms.

The people responsible for registration and reception, apart from Hu Weishi from Mengya, were all previous prize winners who had volunteered to help.

For example, Chen Jiayong, who had received direct admission to Peking University after the first competition, was currently chatting with Hu Weishi.

The six of them headed straight for the New Concept sign. Chen Jiayong immediately understood who they were. "You're here for the competition, right? This way, please."

Chen Guiliang took out his ID card and invitation letter and shook Chen Jiayong's hand. "Hello."

"Hello," Chen Jiayong said with a smile.

The other five were more reserved, greeting him cautiously.

They couldn't figure out who Chen Jiayong was and assumed he was some editor from Mengya magazine.

Chen Jiayong led them to the hotel front desk to check in. Chen Guiliang chose to share a room with Luo Jin. The remaining three boys and one girl couldn't be evenly divided, so they could either get single rooms or be paired with a stranger of the same gender.

After choosing their room numbers and paying the accommodation fee, they went back to register.

The two people handling registration were also previous winners.

Hu Weishi glanced at the registered name and instantly became enthusiastic. "You're Chen Guiliang? I was the one who called you about the semi-finals."

Chen Guiliang smiled and shook her hand. "I thought Sister Weishi would be a middle-aged aunty. I didn't expect you to be so young and beautiful."

This was, of course, just a pleasantry.

Hu Weishi was quite pleased. "Are all of you from Longdu this good with words? The previous contestants all followed Han Han and called me 'Boss'. Only Guo Xiaosi called me Sister Weishi."

"Maybe they find you very approachable," Chen Guiliang replied.

The other five also came over to register. Seeing Chen Guiliang chatting with the editor, they were both surprised and extremely envious.

"Yu Hua, Yu Hua, I've seen his photo!"

Mi Lan exclaimed in a low, excited voice.

Everyone immediately turned to look and saw Yu Hua, wearing a down jacket, walking toward the elevator and chatting cheerfully with four or five other people.

Chen Guiliang suddenly bellowed, "Yu Hua, stop!"

Hearing the shout, Yu Hua turned around in confusion, and the other writers with him also stopped.

Chen Guiliang dragged his suitcase as he ran over, unzipped the side pocket, and pulled out a copy of *To Live* and a marker. "Teacher Yu, my cousin is a big fan of yours. She was in tears begging me to get your autograph."

Yu Hua didn't know whether to laugh or cry as he took the book and pen.

Chen Guiliang continued with his requests, "My cousin's name is Tao Xue. She's in her first year of high school. I hope Teacher Yu can write a few words of blessing for her."

"The 'Tao' with the 'ear' radical, right?" Yu Hua asked as he opened the title page.

Chen Guiliang said, "Yes. And 'Xue' as in snowfall."

Yu Hua quickly wrote a few lines: To classmate Tao Xue, may you be happy every day and make progress in your studies! —Yu Hua.

When returning the book and pen to Chen Guiliang, Yu Hua asked, "Why don't you ask for an autograph for yourself? Don't you like my books?"

Chen Guiliang said, "I don't. They're too painful to read."

"Haha, a lot of people say they're painful," Yu Hua said with a proud laugh.

"Goodbye, teachers."

Chen Guiliang waved and dragged his suitcase back, not even recognizing who the other writers were.

The others who had traveled with him from Sichuan were all dumbfounded.

You could ask for an autograph like that?

It sounded like Chen Guiliang had just yelled, "Yu Hua, stop."

Not only did he use his full name, but it was in an imperative tone.

Stop
